**Reference:** *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), Chapter 6, §6.2. This tutorial uses independent wording, derivations and order data.

## The question we need to answer

The number of packages is discrete, but fulfilment time can be modelled as a continuous variable. The distinction affects how probabilities are computed.

## Formal relationship

$$
P(X=x)=p(x),\qquad P(a\leq T\leq b)=\int_a^b f_T(t)\,dt
$$

The notation makes the assumptions and dependencies explicit. Check that the variables, sets and dimensions match the running example before drawing a conclusion.

## Derive the answer from the example

If X is the item count sampled from our six records, its empirical probabilities are P(X=1)=2/6, P(X=2)=2/6, P(X=3)=2/6. A continuous delivery-time model assigns probability zero to any single exact time, while an interval receives positive probability.

## Interpretation and limitations

A probability density may exceed one at a point; it is the integral that must form a probability. Discrete histograms approximate but do not automatically define a smooth density.

## Explain it yourself

If T is uniform between 5 and 25 minutes, compute P(10≤T≤15).
